summary: Moving to post-quantum cryptography often involves hybrid schemes that combine post-quantum and traditional asymmetric algorithms. This informational RFC defines terminology for such schemes, serving as a reference so documents and discussions about them use consistent words.

eli5.summary: When two kinds of locks are used together, people need shared names for the parts. This is the dictionary for combining new quantum-resistant locks with old ones.

questions: what is a pq/t hybrid scheme
subtitle: A shared dictionary for talking about schemes that combine post-quantum and traditional cryptography.

tldr.problem: Protocols are being changed to resist future quantum computers, and people use words like hybrid, composite and quantum-safe inconsistently.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines terms for algorithms and schemes, cryptographic elements, protocols, desirable properties and certificates, for combinations of post-quantum (PQ) and traditional (T) algorithms.
tldr.outcome: It is a reference so that other documents, standards and organisations use the same words. It has no security impact on Internet protocols by itself.

today: RFC 9794 is an Informational document and has not been obsoleted or updated. The hybrid key exchange design in RFC 9954 cites it for its terminology.

sections.title: Why Hybrids Need Shared Words
sections.content:
Most asymmetric algorithms used on the Internet for key establishment and digital signatures rest on integer factorisation or discrete logarithms. They will be vulnerable to Shor's Algorithm on a sufficiently large quantum computer, called a Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC). Data encrypted today with a vulnerable algorithm can be stored and decrypted later by an attacker with a CRQC.

A designer may therefore combine a post-quantum algorithm with a traditional one, either to add protection against a CRQC or to ease migration. The RFC settles on three terms: post-quantum (PQC), traditional algorithm, and hybrid. It admits that hybrid also describes schemes mixing asymmetric and symmetric algorithms, as in RFC 9180, but keeps it because it is well established in the PQC community.
sections.eli5: One day a super-powerful computer might pick today's locks. So people add new locks next to the old ones, and they need agreed names for this.

sections.title: Schemes and Their Parts
sections.content:
A PQ/T hybrid scheme is a multi-algorithm scheme where at least one component algorithm is post-quantum and at least one is traditional. The components work on the same input and their outputs are used together, serially or in parallel, aiming so that all of them must be broken to break the scheme.

The RFC then names the kinds: a PQ/T hybrid Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM), a PQ/T hybrid Public Key Encryption (PKE) scheme, and a PQ/T hybrid digital signature. A composite scheme is exposed as a single interface of the same type as its components, and a combiner is the method that joins components. A PQ/PQ hybrid uses only post-quantum components.

Section 3 applies the same idea to data. A composite cryptographic element, such as a public key made of two component public keys, is built by a cryptographic element combiner, which could be simple concatenation.
sections.eli5: A hybrid is a team of one new-style and one old-style method working on the same job. A composite is a team that looks like one single member from the outside.

sections.title: Hybrid Protocols: Composite or Not
sections.content:
A PQ/T hybrid protocol uses two or more component algorithms with the same cryptographic functionality, at least one of each type. A protocol that can negotiate either type but not both is not one. Neither is one that mixes functions, such as a post-quantum KEM with a Pre-Shared Key.

In a protocol with composite constructions, the formats of cryptographic elements change while protocol fields and message flow stay largely the same, so most changes land in cryptographic libraries. In a non-composite one, fields, message flow or both change while the elements stay as they are, so most changes land in protocol libraries.

A protocol can mix the two. The RFC says RFC 9370 enables non-composite key establishment for IKEv2.
sections.eli5: Either you swap the lock for a double lock that fits the same door, or you leave the locks alone and change how people walk through the door.

sections.title: Properties You Might Want
sections.content:
No single scheme or protocol can achieve every property. Hybrid confidentiality and hybrid authentication hold as long as at least one component that aims to provide the property stays secure. Hybrid interoperability means the operation completes if both parties support at least one component algorithm.

A scheme alone cannot achieve both interoperability and confidentiality, since confidentiality needs all components used. A protocol can, with downgrade protection outside the cryptographic schemes. Backwards compatibility means success when both parties support the traditional component, using both if both support them. Forwards compatibility means success using a post-quantum component if both support it, with the option to use both.

If the post-quantum component of a hybrid is broken, the scheme stays secure against a classical attacker but is vulnerable to one with a CRQC.
sections.eli5: A double lock is only as strong as its strongest lock. You can also decide whether a guest with only one key should still get in, but then someone could force the weaker way, so you need a guard.

sections.title: Certificates and Chains
sections.content:
A PQ/T hybrid certificate holds public keys for at least one traditional and at least one post-quantum algorithm. A post-quantum certificate or traditional certificate holds a single key of one kind. Chains are defined the same way, and a PQ/T mixed certificate chain contains at least two of the three certificate types.

A PQ/T parallel PKI is two chains, one post-quantum and one traditional, used together in a protocol. Multi-certificate authentication uses two or more end-entity certificates. Using a hybrid certificate does not by itself give hybrid authentication of identity; that depends on the chain of trust.
sections.eli5: An ID card can have two stamps, one old-style and one new-style. But if the office that issued it used only an old-style stamp, the card is no stronger than that.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document defines security-relevant terminology but has no security impact on Internet protocols itself. The security considerations of each PQ/T hybrid protocol belong in that protocol's own specification. General guidance on timelines, benefits and drawbacks of hybrids is out of scope.
sections.eli5: This is only a dictionary, so it does not change how safe anything is. Each real system must explain its own safety.

items.title: Confidentiality
items.text: Holds while at least one relevant component stays secure.

items.title: Authentication
items.text: Holds while at least one relevant component stays secure.

items.title: Interoperability
items.text: Completes if both parties share at least one component.

items.title: Backwards compatibility
items.text: Completes with the traditional component, uses both if available.

items.title: Forwards compatibility
items.text: Completes with the post-quantum component, may use both.
